title: Prefetch decoupler and attention-cost kernel advisor with phase smoother
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:

We observed oscillations in latency for mixed workloads when the scheduler tightly couples prefill admission with decode slot allocation and naive kernel selection. High-attention-density prefill jobs sometimes select kernels with poor short-sequence performance, causing decode contention and propagating backpressure into prefill admission. Conversely, aggressive kernel demotion to prioritize throughput degrades p95 for interactive tenants.

Goal:
- Reduce interactive p95 latency without materially degrading sustained throughput for batch-heavy tenants.
- Introduce a lightweight kernel-advisor service that provides per-request "prefetch hints" derived from attention density, sequence length distribution, and recent kernel performance counters.
- Decouple prefill admission decisions from decode slot allocation via a Phase Smoother that softens sudden rebalances and prevents tenant starvation.

Proposed design:
1) Kernel Advisor (KA):
   - Offline model that maps (model-family, seq_len, attn_density_estimate, batch_size_hint) -> preferred kernel profiles (fast-path vs throughput-path).
   - Expose a simple REST/GRPC hint API consumed by the runtime scheduler: kernel_advisor.suggest(request_sig) -> [kernel_profile, confidence, probe_flag].
   - Probe_flag instructs the scheduler to run a short micro-probe (1-2 iterations) on candidate kernels when confidence is low. Probe results feed back to KA for online calibration.

2) Prefetch Decoupler + Phase Smoother (PDPS):
   - Separate logical stages: Prefill admission (accept/reject + priority) and Decode allocation (slot assignment + kernel_profile).
   - Phase Smoother keeps a short-term moving window (few seconds) of tenant-level weights and enforces hysteresis on weight changes to prevent oscillation from transient kernel selection changes.
   - Introduce tenant_credit buckets to preserve fairness across interactive tenants during bursty periods. Credits refill at a configurable rate tied to SLA tier.

3) Scheduling policy changes:
   - Policy config: latency-focused, balanced, throughput-focused. KA confidence and tenant SLA determine whether to prioritize low-latency kernel or throughput kernel.
   - When KA indicates high attention density and seq_len<64, prefer low-latency kernels; for high seq_len or batch hints, prefer throughput kernels.

Trade-offs considered:
- Micro-probing adds extra work but is bounded and improves kernel assignment accuracy for diverse open-model catalog.
- Decoupling increases scheduler complexity and state to maintain per-tenant windows. Simpler alternatives (single-stage heuristics) cause thrashing.
- Fairness guarantees via credits may reduce peak throughput for greedy tenants but improve perceived latency fairness.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Primary: reduce interactive tier p95 latency by >=10% on mixed workload benchmarks.
- Secondary: throughput (tokens/sec) drop <= 5% for throughput-optimized workloads; fairness index (ratio of p95 between top- and bottom-10% tenants) improves by >15%.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): KA runs in advisory mode; scheduler logs suggestions but ignores them. Collect signals and validate probe behavior. (1 week)
- Phase 2 (opt-in): enable PDPS for a small set of internal tenants/experiments; run A/B comparing balanced vs baseline. (2 weeks)
- Phase 3 (gradual ramp): 10% -> 50% -> 100% with runtime feature flags per region; monitor p95, throughput, error rates. (3+ weeks)

Observability:
- New telemetry: kernel_advisor.suggest_count, probe_success_rate, kernel_switch_rate, tenant_phase_weight, tenant_credit_level. Dashboards and alerts (p95 increase >15% or probe_error_rate >2%).

Implementation tasks (high level):
- KA prototype: data collector for attention_density estimates and kernel perf counters (ENG).
- Scheduler integration: API + PDPS state machine + credits (ENG).
- Simulation harness: add mixed workload generator to existing sim suite and run regressions (ENG/Research).
- Runbook and rollback: API flagging and immediate disable path for any region.

Deliverables:
- Design doc linked below.
- KA dockerized prototype + simple REST endpoint.
- Scheduler patch with feature flag.
- Perf report and rollout checklist.

acceptance_criteria: Kernel Advisor suggests correct kernel profile with >=85% agreement with probe-confirmed winner on held-out workload within 48h of deployment
Interactive p95 improves >=10% for the mixed-workload benchmark at canary scale
No more than 5% regression in sustained throughput for throughput-optimized runs
Feature flag fully disables behavior end-to-end without requiring restarts
